title: Create calendar events and reminders as one lifecycle
testSeam: The scheduling lifecycle's public create interface and its observable event/reminder outcome.
whatToBuild: Creating a calendar event owns any requested reminder as one coherent operation, with a single outcome and no partial schedule.
acceptanceCriteria: Creating an event without a reminder produces the event and no reminder.
Creating an event with a reminder produces both records with the intended relationship and schedule.
If any required part fails, no partial event/reminder state remains.
The lifecycle is testable independently of an HTTP route.

title: Reconcile reminders when calendar events change
testSeam: The scheduling lifecycle's public update interface and its observable reconciled reminder outcome.
whatToBuild: Updating a calendar event reconciles its reminder in the same lifecycle for time changes, reminder changes, removal, and unrelated updates.
acceptanceCriteria: Moving an event recalculates the linked reminder schedule.
Changing reminder intent updates the relationship without duplicates.
Removing reminder intent removes the reminder but preserves the event.
Unrelated event updates leave an unchanged reminder stable.
Failures cannot leave event and reminder schedules inconsistent.

title: Delete calendar events without orphaning reminders
testSeam: The scheduling lifecycle's public delete interface and its observable event/reminder cleanup outcome.
whatToBuild: Deleting a calendar event closes the event/reminder lifecycle in one operation without orphaned reminders or ambiguous partial outcomes.
acceptanceCriteria: Deleting an event with a linked reminder removes both.
Deleting an event without a reminder succeeds without unrelated effects.
Repeated deletion has a defined idempotent outcome.
Failures cannot leave a reminder referring to a missing event.
Lifecycle tests cover create, update, and delete end to end.

title: Deepen authorization-code issuance and exchange
testSeam: The OAuth authorization-code lifecycle's public issue/exchange interface and credential outcome.
whatToBuild: Authorization-code issuance and exchange form one lifecycle binding client, redirect, user, scopes, expiry, and proof-key policy, with one-time consumption.
acceptanceCriteria: Issued codes contain all context required for exchange.
Expired, reused, mismatched, or invalid codes issue no credentials.
A valid code exchanges exactly once for the intended outcome.
Failures are explicit and testable independently of transport adapters.

title: Deepen refresh-token rotation and reuse response
testSeam: The OAuth refresh lifecycle's public rotation interface and family-level reuse outcome.
whatToBuild: Refresh-token use validates context, rotates atomically, and applies a defined token-family response when reuse is detected.
acceptanceCriteria: A valid refresh token produces new access and refresh credentials.
Successful rotation invalidates the prior refresh token atomically.
Reuse is detected and triggers the defined family response.
Invalid refresh tokens never issue credentials.
Concurrent refresh attempts cannot both succeed.

title: Unify access-token issuance and verification
testSeam: The OAuth access-token policy's public issue/verify interface across supported grants.
whatToBuild: All OAuth grants issue access tokens through one policy and consumers verify them through the same claim interpretation.
acceptanceCriteria: Authorization-code and refresh grants use the same required claims.
Verification consistently checks signature, issuer, audience, expiry, subject, and scopes.
Invalid or insufficient tokens map to defined outcomes.
Lifetime and scope policy are centralized and tested.
Valid clients complete issue, refresh, and verify end to end.

title: Route HTTP task writes through a deep Task Writes module
testSeam: The Task Writes module's public intent interface plus the existing HTTP task contract.
whatToBuild: HTTP task creation, updates, completion, and ordering express intent through one behavior owning defaults, placement, synchronization, and persistence outcomes.
acceptanceCriteria: Creation applies established defaults and deterministic placement.
Status and completion remain synchronized on every HTTP write path.
Updates and ordering preserve invariants and return coherent outcomes.
Task-write policy is testable independently of routing and persistence.

title: Give AI task tools identical write behavior
testSeam: Equivalent AI and HTTP task intents observed through the shared Task Writes interface.
whatToBuild: AI task tools use the same Task Writes behavior so defaults, ordering, status, completion, validation, and failure outcomes match HTTP callers.
acceptanceCriteria: AI creation receives the same defaults and placement as HTTP creation.
AI status and completion use the same synchronization rules.
AI validation and persistence failures match domain outcomes.
Parity tests exercise equivalent HTTP and AI intents.
AI adapters own no independent task invariant or ordering policy.

title: Own habit completion, streaks, and milestones together
testSeam: The habit completion behavior's public complete/uncomplete interface and its log, streak, and milestone outcome.
whatToBuild: Completing or uncompleting a habit owns the log, streak, threshold, milestone, retry, and non-critical failure policy together.
acceptanceCriteria: Completion and reversal update logs and streaks consistently.
Crossing a threshold records the correct milestone exactly once.
Retries do not duplicate completion or milestone outcomes.
Milestone failure policy is explicit and testable.
Existing streak and threshold semantics are preserved.

title: Give AI habit logging identical completion behavior
testSeam: Equivalent AI and HTTP habit intents observed through the shared completion interface.
whatToBuild: AI habit logging invokes the same completion behavior so logs, streaks, milestones, retries, and failures match other callers.
acceptanceCriteria: AI completion and reversal match HTTP log and streak outcomes.
AI completion follows the same milestone and deduplication rules.
Retried AI actions create no duplicates.
AI callers observe shared failure outcomes.
Parity tests cover equivalent AI and HTTP intents.

title: Start workouts through a deep routine conversion module
testSeam: The routine-to-workout conversion module's public interface and complete session outcome.
whatToBuild: Starting a workout from a routine maps exercises, targets, sets, and order into a complete session with a single success or failure outcome.
acceptanceCriteria: The workout contains the expected exercise and set mapping.
Exercise order and applicable targets are preserved.
Unsupported source data has a defined failure.
Failed conversion leaves no partial workout state.
Conversion is testable independently of HTTP routing.

title: Save workouts as routines through the same conversion module
testSeam: The workout-to-routine conversion interface plus representative bidirectional round trips.
whatToBuild: Saving a workout as a routine uses the same bidirectional module, infers reusable targets, preserves order, and persists a complete routine.
acceptanceCriteria: Saving creates the expected routine exercises in stable order.
Workout data maps to reusable targets under one policy.
Supported exercise/set types are consistent in both directions.
Invalid data produces no partial routine.
Round-trip tests cover representative cases.

title: Support atomic partial preference updates
testSeam: The profile preference intent interface and its atomic accepted profile outcome.
whatToBuild: Preferences accept validated partial-update intents whose merge and persistence are atomic, preserving unrelated keys under concurrency and failure.
acceptanceCriteria: Only supplied preference keys change.
Invalid values are rejected without partial writes.
Unrelated keys are preserved without caller-side merging.
Concurrent updates cannot silently erase unrelated changes.
All callers receive a consistent profile and cache outcome.

title: Migrate every settings screen to preference intents
testSeam: Each settings surface's user-visible save contract through the shared preference intent interface.
whatToBuild: Every settings surface sends only changed preference intent and no longer chooses persistence paths or performs browser-side read/merge/write.
acceptanceCriteria: All settings surfaces submit only changed keys.
Updating one screen preserves preferences owned by others.
Screens reconcile the same accepted profile and failures.
No settings surface performs its own preference merge.
Existing save, validation, and error behavior remains covered.

title: Create a deep Household Runway Assessment module
testSeam: The Household Runway Assessment module's public input/output interface.
whatToBuild: One assessment outcome owns scenarios, comparisons, adjustments, advice, validation, and result ordering.
acceptanceCriteria: One request returns the complete supported scenario set in stable order.
All comparisons use one interpretation of inputs.
Adjustments and advice derive consistently from the outcome.
Invalid inputs produce defined results or validation failures.
Assessment outcomes are testable independently of callers.

title: Use the assessment for downloads and contract legacy exports
testSeam: Equivalent interactive and downloaded outcomes through the shared assessment interface.
whatToBuild: Downloads and saved/exported representations consume the shared assessment, then obsolete assembly and export paths are removed.
acceptanceCriteria: Interactive, saved, and downloaded results share one assessment outcome.
Downloads contain supported results in stable order.
Equivalent inputs yield semantically identical outputs.
Legacy assembly and obsolete export paths are removed after migration.
Export failures do not alter the assessment.

title: Build Dashboard Snapshots behind one interface
testSeam: The Dashboard Snapshot interface and its complete, degraded, and failed outcomes.
whatToBuild: Dashboard consumers receive one snapshot owning windows, acquisition, enrichment, recurring generation, graceful degradation, and warnings.
acceptanceCriteria: A snapshot returns all required domain information for intended windows.
Enrichment and recurring behavior are applied consistently.
Optional failures degrade predictably with warnings.
Required failures produce a defined failure outcome.
Snapshot tests do not depend on an HTTP route.

title: Persist completed turns for existing conversations
testSeam: The saved-turn interface for an existing conversation and its retry-safe persistence outcome.
whatToBuild: A completed turn owns user and assistant messages, model metadata, retries, and one observable completion or failure outcome.
acceptanceCriteria: Both messages are stored in the correct order.
Assistant model metadata is retained.
Retries do not create duplicate messages.
Partial failures never appear as a successfully saved turn.
The behavior is testable independently of the visual layer.

title: Own first-turn conversation creation and title timing
testSeam: The first saved-turn interface and its conversation, messages, title, and navigation outcome.
whatToBuild: The first completed turn owns conversation creation, messages, metadata, title timing, retry safety, and the navigation identifier.
acceptanceCriteria: The first turn creates one conversation and both messages in order.
Title work happens only after required turn state exists.
The result returns a stable conversation identifier.
Retries do not duplicate conversations, messages, or title work.
Later turns use the existing-conversation lifecycle.

title: Expand a policy-aware authenticated request context
testSeam: The authenticated request-context resolver across explicit credential policies and outcome categories.
whatToBuild: Authenticated requests resolve principal, credential policy, permission, privileged client, and consistent errors while routes declare allowed credentials.
acceptanceCriteria: Cookie, API-key, admin, and MCP credentials obey explicit route policy.
Success returns the required principal, permissions, and client.
Anonymous, invalid, forbidden, and misconfigured outcomes map consistently.
Allowed credentials remain explicit and reviewable.
The context is testable at real adapter boundaries.

title: Migrate productivity request routes
testSeam: Existing productivity HTTP request/response and authorization contracts backed by the new domain interfaces.
whatToBuild: Productivity routes become thin adapters over Task Writes, habit completion, Dashboard Snapshot, and authenticated request context.
acceptanceCriteria: Task and Kanban routes delegate all task-write policy.
Habit routes delegate completion policy.
Dashboard routes map one snapshot outcome consistently.
Routes declare credential policy and consume authenticated context.
Existing contracts and authorization boundaries remain covered.
No duplicate lifecycle or principal-resolution logic remains.

title: Migrate calendar and fitness request routes
testSeam: Existing calendar and fitness HTTP contracts backed by scheduling, conversion, and authenticated-context interfaces.
whatToBuild: Calendar and fitness routes become thin adapters over scheduling lifecycle, bidirectional conversion, and authenticated request context.
acceptanceCriteria: Calendar routes delegate create, update, and delete lifecycles.
Fitness routes delegate both conversion directions.
Routes declare credential policy and consume authenticated context.
Existing contracts and authorization remain covered.
Failures expose no partial scheduling or conversion state.
No duplicate lifecycle, conversion, or principal logic remains.

title: Migrate platform, finance, and chat request routes
testSeam: Existing OAuth, settings, finance, and chat HTTP contracts backed by their completed domain interfaces.
whatToBuild: Platform OAuth, settings/profile, finance, and chat routes become thin adapters over the new lifecycles and authenticated context.
acceptanceCriteria: OAuth routes delegate code, refresh, and access-token lifecycles.
Settings routes accept preference intent without merge policy.
Finance routes and downloads use the shared assessment.
Chat routes delegate existing- and first-turn persistence.
Routes use explicit credential policy and authenticated context.
Existing contracts, retries, and authorization remain covered.
No duplicate lifecycle, assessment, merge, or principal logic remains.

title: Contract legacy authentication plumbing
testSeam: Representative authenticated route contracts across cookie, API-key, admin, and MCP credential policies after contraction.
whatToBuild: Remove superseded route authentication plumbing so policy-aware authenticated context is the sole route-facing mechanism except documented exceptions.
acceptanceCriteria: Legacy helpers and duplicate principal paths have no production callers.
Removal preserves supported credential behavior.
Every authenticated route uses explicit policy and shared context or a tested exception.
Failure mappings remain consistent across route families.
Repository checks and representative end-to-end flows pass.
